uncited: Hierarchical data structures accelerate volume rendering by organizing voxel data into a spatial subdivision hierarchy where internal nodes store aggregate information derived from their children or leaf voxels [Parent].
This structure enables the renderer to prune empty or inactive regions during ray traversal, significantly reducing the number of samples required to generate an image.
Unlike flat grid traversal methods, hierarchical approaches adaptively skip large volumes of empty space, making them particularly effective for sparse or multi-resolution datasets [Parent].
All methods in this family rely on a spatial subdivision hierarchy where internal nodes store aggregate information derived from their children or leaf voxels.
Internal nodes aggregate these properties (e.g., binary occupancy, min/max scalar ranges) from their children.

**Pruning:** During ray traversal, if a node indicates an empty or inactive region (e.g., occupancy flag is 0, or min/max bounds are outside the transfer function's opacity range), the entire subtree is skipped.
**Construction:** The hierarchy is typically constructed bottom-up.
The depth is determined by data dimensions, often requiring padding to powers of two or specific size constraints to maintain regular subdivision [2560-hierarchical-grid-traversal].
This tree is used during rendering to optimize the compositing process, reduce runtime memory consumption, and speed up cell searching for zoom-in viewing.
When a render-node becomes available, the cell with the longest queue is assigned to it.
Each node in the cell-tree has an associated cell ID, and more than one node may have the same cell ID.
A schedule with any combination of non-conflicting link groups is a feasible one, and the optimal schedule for a single render-node includes a maximal group of cache savings links.
The concept of hierarchical spatial subdivision for volume rendering originated in the mid-1990s as a means to handle the computational cost of ray marching through large, sparse datasets.
Early work focused on octrees and kd-trees to skip empty space [Parent].
